title: [YouPass Collect] - Average university students' salaries and tuition fees
prompt: The bar charts give information about the salaries and university fees of students from three universities in two spheres: Law and Business. Summatise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and making comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar charts compare the average salaries and tuition fees, measured in thousands of dollars, for students studying Law and Business at three different universities.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, tuition fees exceeded or matched graduate salaries in most cases across both fields. Additionally, while salary levels were relatively consistent among Law graduates, Business students showed more variation in their expected earnings.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the Law field, Universities A and B reported identical graduate salaries of $40,000, whereas University C recorded a slightly lower figure of $37,500. In terms of tuition fees, University A was the most affordable option, charging $40,000, which was equal to the expected salary. By contrast, University B demanded the highest fees at $60,000, while University C fell in between at $55,000. This means that Law students at University A were the only group whose tuition matched their projected earnings.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Turning to Business studies, graduate salaries varied more significantly across institutions. Universities B and C both offered the highest earning potential at $40,000, while University A lagged behind considerably at just $30,000. Regarding tuition costs, University C charged the most at $60,000, followed by University B at $50,000. University A, despite having the lowest salaries, still required $45,000 in fees, which was $15,000 higher than the expected graduate salary.
